turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in. Have a seat. What can I do for you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been so tired, doctor. Really wiped out. I keep telling myself it's the job and just getting older, I'm fifty-two, but it's starting to frighten me.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been flagging for months. I'm her carer, three mornings a week, and it's obvious.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many months?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, since... it might have been after the summer, or—
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Before Christmas. You were asleep in the armchair in November, more than once.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Was I? Right, months then. And I'm cold all the time, even with the heating right up. Sorry, I'm going on.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight up?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I think so. About a stone, maybe a bit more. My work trousers don't—
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Constipated?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, not really. Only the last couple of weeks, I thought, and I put that down to—
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That's not right. She's been on about her bowels since the autumn. Months, not a fortnight.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between a fortnight and several months. We won't pin it. Mood?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit low, if I'm honest. Flat. I'm an accounts clerk, long hours, and I tell myself anyone would feel like this at fifty-two.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Crying? Loss of enjoyment?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not crying. Just flat. And I wanted to ask you, could this be something nasty, like—
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): One thing at a time. Any chest pain?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not breathless. I did want to ask whether—
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her mum. She was going to say about her mum.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, sorry. My mother had an underactive thyroid. Tablets for years. Is that the sort of thing that runs in families, because I've been reading and—
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you had a thyroid blood test?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Once, yes. Borderline, they said. I can't place when, though. A year, two years? I've no idea.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It wasn't borderline. You showed me the text. The surgery said normal. You've talked yourself into borderline.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Did it say normal? I was sure they'd said borderline. Oh, I might have misread it. And I still couldn't tell you the date.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll repeat it. What medicines are you on?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Omeprazole, twenty milligrams, once a day, for the heartburn. I do forget it some mornings, though, so I'm not sure I take it properly.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I was on citalopram, twenty milligrams, but I stopped it in March. It made me feel woolly. And the GP gave me lactulose for the bowels, but I never took it, not once. It's still in the box.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Vitamin D as well.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, yes. I take vitamin D, once a day. The dose is a thousand units, I think. Maybe. I'm not certain of that.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None that I know of. Should I be worried if I did, or—
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleeping alright?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. It's hard to say. If this is the thyroid, do people get it at my age, and—
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hair thinning?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry? I was still on the other thing, I didn't quite—
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's asking about your hair.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. No, hair's the same. I think. Can it fall out quickly, though? I keep checking the pillow and—
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): You're wandering off again.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. Completely silly, but did you catch the cricket last night? We were stuck on the ring road and it was the only thing on the radio.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): England were poor. That catch at the end, though. She rewound it twice in the car.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): And the weather coming over. Absolute downpour, a white van cutting everyone up. We nearly turned round.
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She had the commentary turned right up. Tea interval and all.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): It was better than sitting there worrying. The neighbour's lad bowls for his school, and he would not stop about the pitch at—
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't follow cricket.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Edgbaston. Whole journey, that was. Pitch, rain, the lot.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Edgbaston, yes. Lovely ground, apparently. We were twenty minutes late with the rain. I am sorry, I know you're rushed.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neck isn't enlarged. Chest is clear. Pulse sixty-eight. Blood pressure one hundred and twenty-eight over eighty-two.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Is sixty-eight too slow? And is that pressure high for fifty-two? I should have asked you that straight away.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Neither is worrying. Tired, cold, weight up, bowels, flat mood, mother with an underactive thyroid. I'd call this a probable underactive thyroid. Provisional. The bloods decide it.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Probable, so it might not be? Could it still be the job and my age? What if the tests come back normal?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we look again. I'm requesting a thyroid function test and a full blood count today.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? Does it hurt? Do I have to fast? And should I start the citalopram again if I'm this flat?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting. Don't restart the citalopram. It's a quick blood test.
[SEG0057] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She'll stew all week if you don't say when we come back.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Book a follow-up with me next week.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Next week even if I perk up a bit? And if I feel worse before then, do I just wait? Sorry, too many questions.
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back sooner if you feel markedly worse, get chest pain, or you can't cope. Otherwise next week. Reception will book it.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Thank you. I won't google all evening. There's more cricket on later, that'll distract me.
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Get the bloods done on your way out.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
